top_choice_rationale: Targeted protein degradation is a new design principle: a bifunctional molecule brings a chosen protein to an E3 ligase so that the cell destroys it, which opens targets with no druggable active site and has been reproduced widely. The trio of Crews and Deshaies (concept and first proof of principle) and Ciulli (structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex cooperativity) is a coherent, defensible allocation for a citation limited to rational bifunctional degraders. The main risks are that no degrader is broadly approved yet and that the glue strand (Handa, Ito, Gray) and Sakamoto and Kim are left out. P002, a mature and clearly attributed achievement, is a sound second choice, and I prefer an award over no award.
